status_summary: Some of the chapter's IRS recommendations have been met by different means and others have moved the opposite way. Congress has rescinded $53.4 billion of the original $79.4 billion in Inflation Reduction Act IRS funding; $31.9 billion of that came in two laws enacted since 2025-01-20 (Public Laws 119-4 and 119-75) and the rest in 2023 and 2024 laws, and TIGTA reports about $26 billion was still available as of 2026-03-31. The FY2026 annual appropriation is about $11.2 billion (TIGTA) versus $12.3 billion in 2025 (BDO), a cut rather than the flat real budget the chapter proposed. IRS headcount fell from over 102,000 in January 2025 to about 74,000 in December 2025 (National Taxpayer Advocate, as reported; TIGTA reports a 28 percent net decrease through January 2026), and GAO found about 17,000 employees resigned or retired early in 2025. On leadership, Treasury created an IRS Chief Executive Officer role on 2025-10-06; after Secretary Bessent's acting-commissioner service under the Vacancies Act expired, the IRS stated on 2026-03-13 that the CEO manages day-to-day operations and reports to the Treasury Secretary. No Senate-confirmed commissioner was found in office as of 2026-10-07, and TIGTA reports senior roles including the CEO were filled by noncompetitive appointments, which is a different design from the statutory presidential appointments the chapter proposes. On specific items, layoff notices went to the IRS equity, diversity and inclusion office in Taxpayer Services in April 2025, but TIGTA reports that court orders canceled those reductions and the employees returned to work, so the chapter's call to close the office was not carried out on that evidence; TIGTA reports 167 IRA-related contracts, mostly IT, were canceled (the chapter asked for an IT contract review), and the Taxpayer Advocate Service lost an estimated 22 to 25 percent of its staff in 2025 (the chapter asked for a budget increase of at least 20 percent). An IT-focused deputy commissioner and a private-sector IT oversight board were not found.

timeline.event: Nextgov reports IRS staff in the Taxpayer Experience Office and the Office of Equity, Diversity and Inclusion in Taxpayer Services received layoff notices the prior Friday. TIGTA later reports (June 2026 snapshot, p. 6) that reduction-in-force notices in April 2025 went to 9 employees in Taxpayer Service's Office of Equity, Diversity, and Inclusion, 179 in the Office of Civil Rights and Compliance and 106 in the Taxpayer Experience Office, and that court orders canceled these reductions and the employees returned to work.
Bloomberg Tax reports the Taxpayer Advocate Service is losing more than 400 employees, about 22 to 25 percent of its staff, mostly through resignation packages, per the National Taxpayer Advocate.

The National Taxpayer Advocate's mid-year report to Congress says the IRS workforce fell from about 102,000 at the start of the 2025 filing season to fewer than 76,000 by June (counting employees on the rolls through 2025-09-30 under early resignation offers), with IT staffing down 27 percent and Taxpayer Services down about 22 percent, and that the administration's FY2026 proposal would keep Taxpayer Services staffing near FY2025 levels. The page does not discuss staffing losses within the Taxpayer Advocate Service.

TIGTA's Major Management Challenges report for FY2026 (posted under an October 2025 path; the first of the month is used because the day is not confirmed) says IRS headcount fell about 25 percent, from roughly 103,000 to 77,000, between January and May 2025, with IT staff down about 25 percent; that 48 senior IT employees were placed on administrative leave in March 2025; that none of 34 legacy case management systems has been retired; and that leadership changed modernization priorities in 2025 and some programs stopped.
timeline.source: Treasury Inspector General for Tax Administration

timeline.event: Treasury announces Frank Bisignano as Chief Executive Officer of the IRS, a newly created role to manage the agency and oversee daily operations, reporting directly to Secretary Bessent; he remains Social Security Commissioner.

Secondary source (Wikipedia, citing the Washington Post; month confirmed, day not): reorganization places sixteen IRS executives, including the Taxpayer Advocate and the acting Chief Counsel, under the CEO.

IRS states that Secretary Bessent's acting-commissioner term under the Vacancies Act has ended, that the Treasury Secretary supervises the IRS, and that the CEO manages day-to-day operations and reports to the Secretary.

GAO report GAO-26-108116 (published 2026-03-16) finds that about 17,047 employees (roughly 17 percent of the January 2025 workforce) left through deferred resignation and early retirement programs in 2025 and that IRS terminated 7,315 probationary employees in February 2025 (reinstated in May 2025; about 60 percent had not returned or had separated by December 2025). It finds the reductions were neither targeted nor strategic, that 1,480 IT employees left by 2025-09-30, that IRS disbanded its Transformation and Strategy Office in March 2025 and paused, redirected or revised some Inflation Reduction Act modernization projects, and recommends a plan for the correspondence backlog, an implementation team for reform efforts and a new strategic workforce plan; the IRS neither agreed nor disagreed.

TIGTA's snapshot report 2026-IE-R009 (issued 2026-06-09) reports 31,273 IRS separations from January 2025 through January 2026 (about 30 percent of the workforce; net decrease 28 percent after about 2,000 hires), 11,330 Taxpayer Services employees lost through 2026-01-10, 2,497 IT employees lost (29 percent), 142 Senior Executive Service members (about 46 percent) separated or took incentives, seven different commissioners during 2025, and an expansion of noncompetitive appointments (not requiring Senate confirmation) to roles including Chief Executive Officer, Chief Financial Officer and Chief of Staff; it does not mention the Taxpayer Advocate Service's staffing.

The FY2025 appropriation of $12.3 billion comes from a BDO article of 2026-01-22 describing a bipartisan funding agreement; enactment details were not separately confirmed, though TIGTA's snapshot gives about $11.2 billion for FY2026. TIGTA gives the total IRA rescission as $53.4 billion in one place and $53.5 billion in another, and the rescissions were made by several measures, some before 2025; which were enacted since 2025-01-20 was not itemized. The January 2026 reorganization and the acting-commissioner dates (the latter now confirmed by the IRS release of 2026-03-13) come from a Wikipedia summary of news reports. The Taxpayer Advocate budget level, whether the National Taxpayer Advocate retains independent personnel authority after the reorganization, and the status of any other equity or diversity office were not verified.
